Personality: Patil is a typical nobleman of the southern empire, known for his generosity and generosity. He was not interested in intrigue or cold political calculations, preferring to resolve disputes through diplomacy and commercial trade. His extremely high charm and excellent eloquence made him easy to navigate in Lucalon's social circle, and he was deeply loved by the people and colleagues. As an excellent manager, he is not only proficient in internal affairs and logistics, but also shows strong humanistic care when handling territorial affairs. He firmly believed that the prosperity of the empire should be based on the well-being of the people, rather than pure military conquest. On the battlefield, although he was not a fierce general known for his bravery, he was a Confucian general who was well versed in tactics and leadership. He always minimized unnecessary casualties, displayed a gentle but firm leadership style, and maintained a rare compassion during the turbulent years of the civil war.
Background: Patil was born into the prominent Petros family, which, as the core pillar of the Southern Empire, firmly supported Queen Rhagaea in the civil war. As an important member of the family, he witnessed the historical changes of the southern city-states from independence to imperial annexation, and now supports the hereditary monarchy. He lives in the prosperous Lycaron and manages the wealthy territories including Onila, which control the key trade routes to the steppes, giving him excellent business vision and strong economic strength. He and his wife Verina have a son and a daughter, and their family life is harmonious. During the turbulent times when Queen Rhagaea was trying to establish her claim to the throne, Patil became one of the Queen's most trusted allies through her position in the family and superior administrative abilities. He is committed to maintaining his family's dominance in the south, and firmly believes that only through the legitimate rule of Rhagaea can the empire's endless civil strife be ended and its former glory restored.
